lines.text: It's nine o'clock PM at Signal Lost studios. Tonight's story, The Cartographer of Smoke, finds RUTH ADLER and TOM BELL with one discovery between them.

lines.speaker: RUTH ADLER
lines.text: Then tell me plainly, because the plain version is the one people deserve.

lines.speaker: TOM BELL
lines.text: The map on this desk is a promise of smoke, and the wind will keep it.

lines.speaker: RUTH ADLER
lines.text: If we sit on this until morning, the morning will arrive without us.

lines.speaker: TOM BELL
lines.text: I want one more reading before anything leaves this room.

lines.speaker: RUTH ADLER
lines.text: One more reading will only tell us what we already know.

lines.speaker: TOM BELL
lines.text: Every number here is a street where somebody has to breathe.

lines.speaker: RUTH ADLER
lines.text: Then we carry it together, and we carry it tonight.

facts.claim: A digitization team preserved more than two thousand Edison wax cylinders recorded between 1888 and 1929, recovering voices and music that had not been heard for a century.
The digitized Edison cylinder collection is open to the public, and archivists continue to restore fragile early recordings before the wax degrades beyond recovery.
